summary: The strongest community photo-editing skill found is `image-edit` in peterkrueck/Claude-Code-Development-Kit (1,383 stars, MIT): Pillow+numpy with bundled deterministic scripts (analyze_bounds.py, crop_image.py) and a complete see-edit-verify loop — Read the image first, measure content bounds with a script, apply the edit, then "Read the output image with the Read tool to visually confirm the result." Second is jezweb/claude-skills' `image-processing` (962 stars, MIT), Pillow-based with a bundled `img-process` CLI covering resize/crop/trim/convert/optimise/thumbnails, but with no visual verification step. ImageMagick-CLI reference skills are the most numerous (1,100+ SKILL.md code-search hits vs ~400 for Pillow), best exemplified by TerminalSkills/skills (Apache-2.0) and einverne/dotfiles (MIT, 658-line guide), but these are command references with no verify loop. ComposioHQ's own image-enhancer — the only editing entry in their 72k-star awesome list — is prompt-only with no toolchain, scripts, or verification. On standardization: raw volume favors ImageMagick CLI, but the best-engineered skills deliberately standardize on Pillow with bundled scripts (jezweb: "Uses Pillow (Python) — no ImageMagick needed"; peterkrueck rejects macOS sips for "unreliable crop offset behavior"); sharp appears mainly as a documented fallback and in auto-generated skill dumps. Exactly one candidate (peterkrueck) closes the loop with the model's vision, and it pairs vision with measurement: verify visually, but never GUESS coordinates visually — measure first. travisvn/awesome-claude-skills contains no photo-editing entries at all.

candidates.name: image-edit (Claude-Code-Development-Kit)
candidates.approach: Local deterministic: Python/Pillow + numpy in a temp venv, with two bundled scripts — analyze_bounds.py (outputs JSON content bounds, padding, suggested square crops) and crop_image.py (composable crop/mirror/rotate/resize). Workflow: Read image visually -> measure bounds with script -> compute coordinates -> apply -> Read output to verify, adjust and re-run.
candidates.description_quote: Edit images with precision — crop, resize, mirror, rotate, trim, and reframe. Use this skill whenever the user asks to crop, resize, trim, mirror, flip, rotate, reframe, or otherwise manipulate an image.

candidates.name: image-processing (jezweb/claude-skills, design-assets plugin)
candidates.approach: Local deterministic: Pillow (Python) via a bundled `img-process` CLI shipped in bin/ (resize, convert, trim, thumbnail, optimise, og-card, batch); generates custom Pillow scripts for compositing/watermarks; documents sips/sharp/ffmpeg as fallbacks. No visual verification step found in SKILL.md.
candidates.description_quote: Process images for web development — resize, crop, trim whitespace, convert formats (PNG/WebP/JPG), optimise file size, generate thumbnails, create OG card images. Uses Pillow (Python) — no ImageMagick needed.

candidates.name: imagemagick (TerminalSkills/skills)
candidates.approach: Local deterministic: ImageMagick CLI (magick/convert/mogrify/composite/identify) expert-prompt style with copy-paste recipes for resize, crop, format conversion, batch watermarking, compositing. No verification loop.
candidates.description_quote: You are an expert in ImageMagick, the powerful command-line tool for creating, editing, compositing, and converting images. You help developers automate image processing pipelines using ImageMagick's `convert`, `mogrify`, `composite`, and `identify` commands — batch resizing, format conversion, watermarking, thumbnail generation, PDF manipulation, and complex image compositing.

candidates.name: imagemagick (einverne/dotfiles)
candidates.approach: Local deterministic: ImageMagick CLI — a 658-line reference covering format conversion, resizing, cropping, effects, watermarks, borders, batch mogrify, geometry syntax, and v7 magick vs legacy convert. No verification loop.
candidates.description_quote: Guide for using ImageMagick command-line tools to perform advanced image processing tasks including format conversion, resizing, cropping, effects, transformations, and batch operations. Use when manipulating images programmatically via shell commands.

candidates.name: image-enhancer (ComposioHQ/awesome-claude-skills)
candidates.approach: Prompt-only: the full 99-line SKILL.md names no library, no script, no API — it describes intents (upscale, sharpen, reduce artifacts, keep originals as backup) and leaves implementation to the model. No verification loop.
candidates.description_quote: Improves the quality of images, especially screenshots, by enhancing resolution, sharpness, and clarity. Perfect for preparing images for presentations, documentation, or social media posts.
candidates.license: not visible in fetched SKILL.md; repo license not verified

findings.claim: The peterkrueck image-edit skill includes an explicit see-edit-verify loop using the model's vision: it opens with a Read-tool inspection and closes with a verify step.
findings.quote: Step 5 — Verify ... Read the output image with the Read tool to visually confirm the result. If it doesn't look right, adjust and re-run — the original is untouched.

findings.claim: The same skill pairs vision with measurement rather than trusting vision for coordinates — its core rule is measure-before-cut via a bundled analysis script.
findings.quote: Never guess crop coordinates from visual inspection. Images routinely have large invisible regions — transparent padding, solid-color borders, or dead space — that make visual estimates wildly wrong.

findings.claim: The best-engineered editing skills standardize on Pillow with bundled deterministic scripts, explicitly avoiding ImageMagick/sips; peterkrueck justifies Pillow over sips.
findings.quote: Precision image manipulation using Python/Pillow. This skill exists because macOS `sips` has unreliable crop offset behavior and visual inspection alone leads to bad coordinates

findings.claim: jezweb's image-processing skill also standardizes on Pillow and positions sharp (npm) only as a fallback alongside sips and ffmpeg.

By raw volume, ImageMagick CLI is the most common toolchain in community SKILL.md files: GitHub code search returned total_count 1,142 for 'filename:SKILL.md ImageMagick crop resize' vs 412 for 'filename:SKILL.md Pillow resize watermark'; sharp hits are dominated by auto-generated dumps (agentskillexchange/skills, majiayu000/claude-skill-registry).
findings.source_url: https://api.github.com/search/code (queries: filename:SKILL.md ImageMagick crop resize; filename:SKILL.md Pillow resize watermark)

findings.claim: ComposioHQ's image-enhancer — the only photo-editing entry in the 72k-star ComposioHQ awesome list — is prompt-only: the full SKILL.md names no library, script, or API and contains no verification step.
findings.quote: This skill takes your images and screenshots and makes them look better—sharper, clearer, and more professional.

findings.claim: travisvn/awesome-claude-skills lists no photo/image-editing skills — only generation-adjacent entries (algorithmic-art, canvas-design, slack-gif-creator, web-asset-generator).

Neither of the two comprehensive ImageMagick reference skills (TerminalSkills/skills, einverne/dotfiles) contains any visual-verification or look-at-the-result instruction (grep for verify/visual/inspect/feedback over full downloaded files found none in workflow context).

Search results for image-editing SKILL.md files are heavily polluted by aggregator mirrors (majiayu000/claude-skill-registry, aiskillstore/marketplace, agentskillexchange/skills, ComeOnOliver/skillshub) that republish other authors' skills under renamed paths — originals should be preferred for provenance.
SamurAIGPT/Generative-Media-Skills contains a core/edit SKILL.md, but the repo name indicates generative-media API orientation (sibling researcher's scope); not fetched or evaluated.

bounds: Not checked: skillsmp.com (egress proxy blocked the domain), claudemarketplaces.com and claudeskills.info (fetch budget exhausted ~12 network fetches). GitHub MCP get_file_contents and direct api.github.com/repos calls were restricted to the session repo (403), so file contents came from raw.githubusercontent.com and stars/licenses from the GitHub search API plus raw LICENSE files; ComposioHQ repo license not determined. Star counts are repo-level, never per-skill — image-enhancer inherits the 72k-star awesome list, not its own popularity. I did not download the bundled scripts (analyze_bounds.py, crop_image.py, img-process) to confirm they exist and run — only the SKILL.md text referencing them. The two awesome-list scans were WebFetch page fetches summarized by a small model, so an obscure editing entry could have been missed. Code search sampled top ~30 results of 1,100-4,600 total per query across five keyword combinations (ImageMagick, Pillow, sharp, background removal, vision-verify phrasings); niche skills using other toolchains (OpenCV, GraphicsMagick, rembg) were not specifically searched. The yangruihan pillow image-edit-skill seen in an OpenClaw marketplace mirror could not be traced to an original repo (user search 422'd). Toolchain-count comparison (1,142 vs 412) uses raw GitHub total_count, which includes duplicates and mirrors.
